item.title: Moscow spokeswoman mocks EU diplomat over freezing Kyiv conditions
item.description: The head of the EU delegation in Kyiv, Katarína Mathernová, says the Ukrainian capital is facing a winter humanitarian catastrophe, due to Russian attacks on the heating supplies.

item.title: EU says ‘concerns’ raised with UAE over its role in Sudan war
item.description: The EU says it has challenged the UAE over its role in Sudan's civil war, despite being in trade talks with Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Israel’s ‘de facto annexation’ of West Bank earns only mild EU rebuke
item.description: Israel pledged to "kill" the EU and UN-backed two-state solution to the Arab-Israeli conflict, as EU "condemned" new anti-Palestinian laws.

item.title: Why Bangladesh’s election is key moment for EU leverage to protect journalists
item.description: Bangladesh remains one of Asia’s leading jailers of journalists — with it's election on Thursday, and Brussels negotiating a Partnership and Cooperation Agreement (the bloc’s first with a South Asian nation), the EU has never been in a stronger position, writes the Committee to Protect Journalists.

item.title: Listen: Italian PM Meloni mirrors Trump’s style amid Winter Olympic clash
item.description: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni calls Winter Olympics protesters "enemies of Italy," echoing Trump’s divisive playbook. Is Europe witnessing the rise of ‘Trumpification’ in Italian politics?

item.title: France, Sweden and UK worsen in annual global corruption index
item.description: The 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index from NGO Transparency International, has found that global corruption is worse than a decade ago, with democracies particularly slipping.

item.title: Europe’s democratic winter — How EU leaders impose deregulation, bypassing citizens and MEPs
item.description: At their 'leaders' retreat', we are seeing the curtailing of EU democracy in the name of saving Europe’s economy. They should be unleashing citizens' demand for a stronger, independent Europe.

item.title: UN ‘faces financial collapse by July,’ Baerbock warns MEPs
item.description: The United Nations faces financial collapse in July, said Annalena Baerbock, the German former foreign minister who now presides over the UN general assembly.

item.title: Russian chess boss, Central Asia, crypto targeted in new EU sanctions
item.description: Russia's world chess king and Asian sanctions-busters feature in the draft new round of EU measures, which also cover chemical weapons, killer drones, mercenaries in Belize, bitcoins, and salt.

item.title: MEPs approve ‘safeguards’ to halt cheap Mercosur imports if EU farmers suffer
item.description: MEPs say the so-called 'safeguards' regulation will ensure European farmers are not put out of business by cheap imports from South America.
